sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2016; PDF dated 2011]. The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List. Circulation draft, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge. 16 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Table 1 (p.1) gives ALCAM (120-word survey list) as the only source for Evant; p.2 sec.3: 'For Tivoid languages, phonologies of any sort exist for only three languages, Tiv, Esimbi and Ugarə.' The only prosodic remark (p.2) is 'Tiv and Ugarə are two-tone languages.. Esimbi has three tones'; Evand appears only as an untone-marked wordlist column and in the Central Tivoid A subgrouping.

sources.citation: Dieu, Michel & Patrick Renaud (eds.). 1983. Situation linguistique en Afrique centrale. Inventaire preliminaire: le Cameroun (Atlas linguistique de l'Afrique centrale / Atlas linguistique du Cameroun, ALCAM). Paris: ACCT; Yaounde: CERDOTOLA / DGRST. 475 pp. [Evand = language 896, pp. 120-121; status table p. ~163; index]
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. The Evand entry (pp.120-121) gives only location, administrative grouping ('asumbo' canton with iyive, iceve, ipulo, eman, ihatum), and affiliation ('iyive, iceve et evand soient assez proches du tiv' per the 1983 Breton-Nseme mission); the standardisation-status table marks evand '-' for 'Et. ling.' (no linguistic study). The 120-word ALCAM survey list for 896 is not printed in this volume, so there are not even tone-marked forms here.
